asof: Settles Thu 19 Nov 2026 · written Fri 20 Nov
headline: Soft Philly Fed and claims plus IPO jitters rally the strip up to 5.5bp; U7 peak 4.68%, about three hikes.
summary: SR3 bull-steepened at the front and rallied most through the peak: U7, Z7 and H8 fell 5.5bp in rate to 4.68%, 4.64% and 4.59%, M7 5bp to 4.66%, H7 3.5bp to 4.54% and Z6 only 1.3bp to 4.287%, with Z8 4bp lower at 4.505% and U6 unchanged at 3.9325%. On the week Z6 is 1.8bp lower but U7 14bp, Z7 16bp and M8–U8 18bp lower; from the 30 October settle H7 through U7 are still 16–18.5bp higher, Z6 14.2bp and Z9 9bp. U7 remains the peak at 4.68%, 78bp over the 3.90% SOFR fixing, with 19.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9. That is about three hikes, in line with JPMorgan's new December, January and March call and above the two many economists, including Pantheon, expect.
drivers: Soft claims and Philly Fed pull out later hikes

The Philly Fed index fell to 6.3 against 20 expected, with new orders at −0.4, though prices paid jumped to 58.2. Initial claims rose to 203k against 197k and continuing claims 70k to 1.763m, the highest since late August; M7 to H8 fell 5–5.5bp while Z6 slipped only 1.3bp.
Anthropic IPO swing triggers a haven bid

Anthropic opened at $111.50 against an $83 IPO price but slipped below $100, and the equity selloff that followed sent Treasury yields 1–4bp lower, led by the front end and belly. Z6/H7 fell 2.2bp to +25.3bp and Z6/M7 3.7bp to +37.3bp.
Fed speakers keep December locked in

Goolsbee said inflation is not on a path back to 2% and the AI boom risks overheating; Jefferson said the buildout is pushing up demand and inflation, and Barr backed further hikes on Wednesday. The front held: U6 was unchanged and Wednesday's fed funds futures priced 27.5bp for 9 December, with Thursday's FedWatch near 95% for 25bp and 5% for 50bp.
Supply and funding calm; oil flat

The $19bn 10-year TIPS tailed just 0.3bp against a 1.9bp six-auction average, ahead of $69bn 2s, $70bn 5s and $44bn 7s next week. SOFR fixed at 3.90% on 18 November, down 2bp and 2bp over EFFR at 3.88%; Brent settled 3 cents higher at $91.98 and WTI 5 cents lower at $83.21, its lowest since 26 August.
spreads: The front flattened as the rally ran from H7 back. U6/Z6 fell 1.3bp to +35.45bp (+13.2bp on the month), Z6/H7 2.2bp to +25.3bp (−4.2bp week-to-date, +4.3bp on the month) and H7/M7 1.5bp to +12bp (−5bp on the week, −0.5bp on the month), while M7/U7 slipped 0.5bp to +2bp. Past the peak U7/Z7 held at −4bp, Z7/H8 at −5bp and H8/M8 at −4bp, while the 2028–29 spreads were flat to 1bp higher at between −2.5bp and 0 as Z8 and beyond lagged. Z6/Z7 fell 4.2bp to +35.3bp (−14.2bp on the week, +0.3bp on the month) and Z6/M7 3.7bp to +37.3bp (−9.2bp on the week, +3.8bp on the month); Z7/Z8 rose 1.5bp to −13.5bp (−6bp on the month), U7/Z8 1.5bp to −17.5bp (−3.5bp on the week, −7.5bp on the month) and Z8/Z9 1bp to −2bp. The H7/M7/U7 fly fell 1bp to +10bp (−2bp on the week, +1.5bp on the month) and M7/U7/Z7 0.5bp to +6bp (−0.5bp on the month).
fed: The latest weekday fed funds futures snapshot, Wednesday's after the minutes, prices 27.5bp for 9 December (90.1% for 25bp, 9.9% for 50bp), 44.5bp by January, 61.1bp by March, 76.1bp by June and an 80bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.68%), easing to 75bp by December 2027. That compares with 26.1bp, 43bp, 59.6bp, 74.1bp and a 78.5bp peak on Tuesday, 28.9bp, 44.5bp, 62.2bp, 77.1bp and 81bp a week earlier on 11 November, and 17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp and 57bp at the 30 October month-end: December is up 9.9bp on the month and the peak 23bp, but the peak is 1bp below a week ago. Adding the 2bp SOFR–EFFR gap, Wednesday's ZQ path implies 4.265% for Z6's December–March window, 4.55% for H7 and 4.69% for U7, so after Thursday's rally Z6 at 4.287% sits 2bp above it and H7 and U7 1bp below. JPMorgan now expects hikes in December, January and March and Pantheon only December and January, while Waller wants last year's three cuts reversed and possibly more; the strip's 78bp peak over SOFR matches the three-hike camp.

ideas.title: Z6/M7: lower the re-sell order to +40bp
ideas.trade: Sell SR3Z6, buy SR3M7 (sell the Z6/M7 spread) at +40bp
ideas.why: The +42bp order never filled: the spread settled at +41bp on Wednesday and fell 3.7bp to +37.3bp as M7 rallied 5bp on the soft data, 9.2bp lower on the week. We lower the order to +40bp rather than chase: hikes are locked in for December and January (44.5bp in ZQ) while weaker orders and rising claims cap what M7 can add. From +40bp it is 6bp to target against 4bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: A hot PCE or a strong November payrolls report could reprice mid-2027 hikes faster than Z6 and push the spread through +44bp.

ideas.title: Hold long Z6/H7 into PCE
ideas.trade: Buy SR3Z6, sell SR3H7 (buy the Z6/H7 spread)
ideas.why: Open and 0.7bp against us: Z6/H7 fell 2.2bp to +25.3bp as H7 rallied 3.5bp against 1.3bp in Z6 on the soft data. Wednesday's ZQ path prices 33.6bp across the January and March meetings, while JPMorgan now forecasts a hike at each and Goolsbee and Jefferson flagged AI-driven demand pressure. From here it is 6.7bp to target and 3.3bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: Another weak data run into PCE could take March out of the price and push the spread below +22bp.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract into bill settlement and month-end

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 was unchanged at 3.9325% for a second day while SOFR fixed at 3.90% on 18 November, down 2bp but still 2bp over EFFR at 3.88%. Only its last week follows the 9 December decision, where Wednesday's ZQ priced a 9.9% chance of 50bp, and $300bn of bills settle on 24 November before $183bn of coupons settle on month-end.
ideas.risk: If month-end passes quietly and SOFR slips to 3.88%, U6 would gain a couple of bp.
